newsitem.title: POLAND: Wroclaw flood damage may not alter merger.
newsitem.headline: Wroclaw flood damage may not alter merger.

text.p: Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund Co said that if paint firm Polifarb Wroclaw's 1997 net profit forecast downward revision proves true it still may not demand changes in conditions of the planned merger with Polifarb Cieszyn.
Pioneer holds about 10 percent of Cieszyn.

Pioneer's investment head Jaroslaw Skorulski told Reuters on Monday that if Wroclaw's statement last week proved true -- that Wroclaw's 11.6 million zlotys in flood damage were covered by insurer PZU -- merger conditions might not need be changed.
Over the weekend a Polish newspaper questioned whether the losses were fully covered, an allegation Wroclaw's president denied in another paper.

"If those losses are covered by PZU, if the property losses are not that big, I think...the merger would then be possible at similar conditions as was approved," Skorulski said, adding that he would also like to inspect the plant in Wroclaw.
Polifarb Wroclaw last week lowered its 1997 net profit forecast by 10.2 percent to 20.2 million zlotys due to floods.
Polifarb Cieszyn has said it incurred about one million zlotys in flood damage.
Earlier this year Polifarb Cieszyn's shareholders decided that they should get 53.5 percent of the new firm in this year's planned merger with Wroclaw, altering the previous plan of a 50-50 merger.
